tell: An anticonvulsant that induces its own metabolism, so its half-life falls from 25 to 65 hours to 12 to 17 hours over weeks of dosing.

clues.text: The suspension delivers the same total drug to the circulation as the tablets, only absorbed somewhat faster. It is 76% bound to plasma proteins, and 72% of a dose is excreted in urine, mostly as metabolites.
The active moiety has a molecular weight of 236.27 and is a white to off-white powder, practically insoluble in water but soluble in alcohol and acetone.
Approved under an NDA as a 100 mg per 5 mL oral suspension.
Boxed warning for serious skin reactions linked to the HLA-B*1502 allele. Contraindicated after bone marrow depression or tricyclic sensitivity; dizziness and drowsiness are common.
Epilepsy, including partial seizures and generalized tonic-clonic seizures, and the pain of true trigeminal neuralgia.
The mechanism is unknown; it appears to reduce polysynaptic responses and block post-tetanic potentiation, and it is chemically unrelated to other drugs of its use.
The generic name begins with C and has thirteen letters.
